newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada poll shows Bloc weakens in Quebec.
newsitem.headline: Canada poll shows Bloc weakens in Quebec.

text.p: A poll broadcast on the Canadian Broadcasting Corp on Monday showed weakening support for the separatist Bloc Quebecois and a surge in support for the Conservatives in Quebec ahead of a June 2 federal election.
The CROP poll showed support for the ruling Liberals at 37 percent, the Bloc at 35 percent and the Conservatives at 25 percent after a distribution of undecided voters.

Before the distribution, the split was Liberals 30 percent, Bloc 29 percent, Conservatives 20 percent, New Democrats two percent, Reform Party one percent and undecided 17 percent, said Montreal French-language daily newspaper La Presse, which also published the poll.
Liberal Prime Minister Jean Chretien on Sunday called a Canadian election for June 2.
"If the federal election were held today, the Bloc Quebecois and the Liberal Party would be at even strength in Quebec and the Conservative Party would make a stunning breakthrough," La Presse said.

The CROP poll shows a "spectacular rebound" for the Tories in Quebec, CROP vice-president Claude Gauthier told La Presse. Quebec voter support for the Tories was at only three percent in February 1995 and seven percent in February 1996.

The apparent rebound in Tory electoral fortunes in Quebec was due to the popularity of Conservative leader Jean Charest, a bilingual Quebecker who is the most popular of federal party leaders in Quebec, La Presse said.
In the CROP poll, 34 percent of Quebec voters thought Charest would make the best prime minister, compared with 24 percent for Chretien and 11 percent for Bloc leader Gilles Duceppe.

The CROP poll was a national poll of 2,514 respondents across Canada aged 18 years and over, of which 918 where in Quebec. The poll's margin of error for the Quebec portion was three percent, 19 times out of 20.
The CROP poll's national results will be released on Tuesday.

The CROP poll underscores a trend revealed in a SOM Inc poll published in La Presse on Saturday, which showed the popularity of the separatist Bloc narrowing and the Conservatives getting stronger in Quebec.
After redistribution of undecided voters, the SOM poll showed Bloc support at 40 percent, compared with 35 percent for the Liberals and 19 percent for the Conservatives.
"This polls shows a Bloc fairly weaker than surveys conducted by other pollsters over the last weeks, while the Liberal Party is about at the same point," La Presse said.

The SOM poll of 1,001 respondents drawn from a representative sample of the Quebec population was conducted by telephone April 18 to 23. The poll had a margin of error of 3.7 percent 19 times out of 20.
